name: Cinematic Human Behavior World v2
tone: mature adult psychology-documentary editorial graphic-novel illustration

creativeTranslation.principle: do not prompt the psychology; prompt observable evidence of the psychology
creativeTranslation.flowAgentRole: production executor, not autonomous art director

character.recognitionTest: if the silhouette could pass as a thin normal cartoon human, it is wrong; it must unmistakably read as an illustrated stick figure
character.head: one simple circle or slightly vertical oval; not chibi oversized; no realistic skull or jaw
character.face: two tiny dot/short-mark eyes, one tiny mouth line, optional tiny eyebrow strokes; no nose, ears, cheeks, eyelids or realistic facial construction
character.torso: one tiny narrow graphic clothing shape clearly below half the head width; no chest, waist, hips or anatomical shoulder mass
character.arms: ultra-thin near-uniform line-like strokes; no upper-arm, forearm or sleeve volume
character.legs: ultra-thin near-uniform line-like strokes; no thigh, calf, hip-to-thigh or trouser-leg volume
character.hands: tiny endpoint/dot/mitten shapes only; no fingers
character.clothing: flat graphic cue only; never create shoulders, chest, sleeves, waist, hips, thighs or calves
character.hair: tiny flat head-edge cue only; no volumetric hairstyle

characterPresence.rule: use humans only when action, reaction, hierarchy or relationship is the clearest explanation

representationVariety.rule: choose the clearest visual form per beat; do not force character scenes, text cards, schemas, montage, split or group scenes

moodEngine.rule: mood changes lighting, framing, posture, negative space, saturation and temperature but never changes the illustration family or geometric anatomy

world.locations: believable everyday, social, institutional, commercial, financial, night and tense environments chosen for the beat
world.lighting: adaptive motivated cinematic illustrated lighting; lighting supports concrete action instead of replacing it with symbolism
world.shading: soft cel shading with stronger graphic shadows when mood requires

rules: no grey beige cream wash as default
strongest useful contrast on focal subject
mood mode influences saturation and temperature
do not repeat identical teal-and-cream balance across the video
do not mechanically repeat red burgundy dark treatment across the whole video
use local environment colors and beat-specific lighting when useful
color never replaces observable behavior or composition

hardFails: bare line stickman or whiteboard doodle
cute chibi mascot or toy-like character
broad shoulders or normal cartoon-human body mass
chest waist hip thigh or calf anatomy
background people using thicker or different anatomy
abstract psychology instruction replaces concrete observable evidence
effect name is literalized only because of its wording
symbolic glow ray or icon replaces clearer real-world behavior
multiple scene numbers combined into one storyboard/contact-sheet asset
